title: SSA Says White Plains Hearing-Office Closure Decision Dates to December 2024
description_short: SSA said no local field offices had been permanently closed since Jan. 1, 2025, and dated the White Plains hearing-office decision to December 2024.
description_medium: On March 27, 2025, the Social Security Administration said it had not permanently closed or announced the permanent closure of any local field office since Jan. 1. SSA distinguished those sites from one permanent hearing-office closure in White Plains, New York, and said most lease-termination sites were small hearing rooms without assigned employees. In October, SSA said the White Plains decision was made in December 2024 by the previous administration.
description_long: On March 27, 2025, the Social Security Administration issued a correction about reports that it was permanently closing local field offices. SSA said that since January 1 it had not permanently closed or announced the permanent closure of any local field office. It distinguished those offices from one hearing office in White Plains, New York, whose permanent closure it had announced. The agency also said most sites it had sent to the General Services Administration for possible lease termination were small hearing rooms with no assigned employees. In an October 31 release, SSA said the White Plains hearing-office closure had been chosen in December 2024 by the previous administration. The release described a West Nyack hearing space intended to add in-person options for Hudson Valley claimants. This card records SSA’s clarification and the disclosed timeline. It does not claim that DOGE closed ten field offices in February. SSA’s releases do not substantiate the original item’s 135-mile travel figure, seven-county service count, 2,000-case backlog, or specific travel impacts on disabled and elderly beneficiaries; those claims are omitted.

title: Unverified Claim of February Arrest Threats Against Milley and Esper
description_short: The supplied record alleges February 2025 arrest threats against Mark Milley and Mark Esper; the cited material does not establish them.
description_medium: The supplied record alleges that Trump and senior White House officials threatened in February 2025 to arrest and prosecute Mark Milley and Mark Esper over criticism. The supplied AP citation concerns different actions against Milley: a security-detail and clearance revocation and an inspector-general review. It does not document the alleged arrest threat or establish a matching threat against Esper. Keep the allegation attributed and internal pending direct evidence.
description_long: Internal draft only. The supplied card alleges that President Donald Trump and senior White House officials threatened in February 2025 to arrest and prosecute retired Gen. Mark Milley and former Defense Secretary Mark Esper because they had criticized Trump. It further attributes a chilling effect to the alleged threats and says both men would not be intimidated. The supplied evidence does not substantiate those statements: its cited Associated Press article reports Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth revoking Milley's security detail and clearance and ordering a review by the Pentagon inspector general. Those are reported actions, not a documented arrest threat; the accessed AP excerpt does not establish an equivalent action or threat against Esper. The original input also says Milley and Esper had criticized Trump, but it supplies no source excerpt for those statements or the alleged February threat. Keep the arrest allegation clearly attributed, separate it from the reported security and clearance actions, and leave publication blocked until a direct statement or reliable contemporaneous report documents the claimed threat. The AP article's silence on an arrest threat is not evidence that no such statement occurred.

title: Unverified February Claim of a University Tax-Exemption Threat
description_short: The supplied record alleges a Feb. 15, 2025 tax-status threat to universities; its date and scope are not established.
description_medium: The supplied record alleges that Trump posted on February 15, 2025, threatening universities' tax-exempt status over DEI, protest policies, and faculty governance. The packet supplies no matching post or source excerpt. Separate February reporting concerns an Education Department funding warning over DEI, while later reporting concerns Harvard specifically. Neither establishes the supplied February tax-status claim, so this remains an internal, unverified draft.
description_long: Internal draft only. The supplied card alleges that Donald Trump posted on February 15, 2025, threatening to revoke the tax-exempt status of universities that rejected administration demands concerning DEI, campus protest policies, and faculty governance. The packet contains no original post URL or source excerpt establishing that date, broad university scope, or the stated conditions. Search excerpts surfaced separate February reporting about an Education Department warning that institutions could lose federal funding over DEI, and April reporting about a Harvard-specific tax-status threat. Those reports concern different actions, dates, and scopes; they do not verify this allegation and are not substituted as the event. The supplied text also asserts that endowments worth tens of billions of dollars could be exposed, that research programs faced severe consequences, that legal scholars identified First Amendment problems, that university boards held emergency reviews, and that the threat sent shockwaves through higher education. The packet supplies no supporting excerpts for those details. Preserve the alleged February claim only as attributed, with its date and scope marked uncertain. Publication requires a matching original post or reliable contemporaneous report and source review.

title: Trump Order Calls for Immigration Detention Pending Proceedings, Subject to Law
description_short: Trump's Jan. 20 order directs detention of removable immigrants pending proceedings or removal, to the extent permitted by law.
description_medium: Section 10 of the Jan. 20, 2025 order directs DHS to use or establish detention facilities and to detain people apprehended for immigration-law violations pending removal proceedings or removal, to the extent permitted by law. That text supports a detention directive; it does not itself establish indefinite detention without charge, denied bail hearings, or immediate court blocks.
description_long: On January 20, 2025, President Donald Trump issued Executive Order 14159, “Protecting the American People Against Invasion.” Section 10 directs the Homeland Security secretary to take appropriate action and use legally available resources or contracts for facilities to detain removable immigrants. It further directs detention of people apprehended for immigration-law violations while removal proceedings are pending or until removal, “to the extent permitted by law.” The order therefore supports describing a federal detention directive tied to removal proceedings and an express legal limitation. The text does not itself say that immigrants may be held indefinitely without charges, instruct immigration judges to deny bail hearings, or report that federal judges immediately blocked the order. The supplied card made those additional claims without providing a court ruling or other supporting source; they are omitted here. The order’s language alone also does not establish how long anyone was detained, how many people were affected, what agencies implemented, or how a court later ruled. This corrected entry records what the signed order says without turning its detention language into unsupported claims about custody duration, court action, or a legal finding.
